newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Fresh violence erupts in French Guiana.
newsitem.headline: Fresh violence erupts in French Guiana.

text.p: Fresh violence erupted late on Tuesday in French Guiana after police arrested three more members of the territory's independence movement in the latest crackdown, witnesses said.
Para-military riot police flown in from France clashed with demonstrators for the second time in a week in the capital Cayenne as night fell.
Police protecting the town's central police station and courthouse on the city's central boulevard started firing teargas grenades at 7.15 pm local time (2215 GMT) to disperse crowds.
The boulevard had been closed by police since early morning and several hundred police were surrounding key government buildings.
Earlier Tuesday police arrested Jean-Victor Castor and Fabien Canavy, both members of the Guiana Workers Union (UTG).
Jean-Claude Ringuet, a member of the Guiana National Popular Party (PNPG), gave himself up to police after taking refuge for several hours in Cayenne's town hall.
French officials pledged last week to crack down on violence in its South American overseas territory after a new wave of violence last Thursday left two police wounded and several shops ransacked.
The latest violence was triggered by a series of detentions, including that of Alain Michel a founding member of the PNPG.
Michel was detained on April 11 and taken the next day with four others to the French Caribbean island of Martinique aboard a military aircraft.

He was charged with arson and violence against a magistrate when the residence of French Guiana's state prosecutor was attacked last November in a previous wave of riots in which one person was killed and millions of dollars worth of property was damaged.
French officials described those riots as "a deliberate attempt to destabilise French Guiana."
Eight people have been arrested in connection with the attack on the prosecutor's home.

French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent territory in the Western Hemisphere mainland. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
